listing.name: Planetary-Sector 0.0.1: Total Ground Sim Overhaul mod hub. (pre-alpha)

description:
Dual Elevation
Ground and orbital combat on the same battlefield, plus a full command and intel overhaul
Work in progress - alpha - Starsector 0.98a - current internal build 0.33.3.1

Download: not yet released. This thread tracks progress; a GitHub release with source will be linked here.
Source: GitHub (when public)

Requirements:

LazyLib (required)
Nexerelin (strongly recommended: Dual Elevation takes over Nexerelin invasions and raids)

Save compatibility: alpha. Use a new or test save. Removing the mod mid-campaign is not supported, and versions may break saves.

Planned split: two mods
The project has grown past "ground combat". Before public release it will most likely be split in two:

A standalone Command & Intel mod: battlegroups, command points, the intel grade ladder, electronic warfare, morale, the new Tab map and the campaign sensor cone. It works on its own with vanilla space combat.
Dual Elevation (possibly renamed Planetary-Sector): the ground combat overhaul. It requires and builds on the Command & Intel mod.

Names and boundaries aren't final yet. Feedback welcome.

Ground combat
Battles around planets spawn a ground map below the orbital fight. Terrain, buildings and ruins come from the planet type, size, conditions and colony state. Space ships fight in orbit, ground units fight on the surface, and each layer can fire at the other.

Drop zones: space capture points are drop zones. Hold one with your ships and you can land or recall ground units through it. You do not have to win the orbital fight, only hold a zone.
Transports carry the army: ground units go down and come back up aboard ships inside a held zone. Each hull carries what its cargo hold and spare crew berths allow, and troop transports carry double. Big armoured haulers get a real combat job.
Loot has to be hauled: captured buildings and dig sites leave loot on the ground. Your ships haul it to orbit during the fight; anything left behind is kept only if you hold orbit at the end.
Two deployment menus: the vanilla deploy screen is for space ships; ground units deploy from their own panel, and units that lift off can go down again in the same battle.
Battles do not auto-end: winning orbit lets you end the engagement with ship recovery priority, or keep fighting on the ground.
Invasion footholds: troops left on the surface keep fighting offscreen and are already landed when you return.
Ruins expeditions: land a ground force on a ruins world, dig the sites and hold off the derelict drones and Domain sentries they wake. No marines needed.
Stations sit above the spaceport drop zone.
Ground units are ships that travel between planets mothballed and are repaired for supplies when deployed, standing in for the supply cost of vanilla invasions.
Ground roster: 183 designs across low/mid/high-tech plus faction sets (including Remnant, Derelict and Hiver), with animated walker legs, tank treads and wheels. Mecha frames from mods like armaa and Diable drop from orbit.
Planet-built maps: 13 biomes, and all vanilla colony conditions map to terrain and rules, with buildings that ruin in stages and hulks deorbiting mid-fight.

Command & Intel

Battlegroups: officers lead battlegroups sized by their level, in Recon, Support, Assault or Defense stance. Officer skills now shape command points, recon, EW, cohesion and logistics. Second-in-Command is supported through an optional bridge.
Command points: every order costs CP. Regen depends on your flagship, comm relays, intel, morale and jamming.
New Tab map: replaces the vanilla Tab map and the old ` command view. Give battlegroup and ground orders with Recon, Support, Assault and Defense lenses. It only shows what your side actually knows.
8-grade intel: contacts climb from a faint signature to a bearing, a position, a lock and finally full intent. You need a lock to fire guided weapons, and contacts fade if you stop tracking them. The AI plays by the same rules.
Electronic warfare: go dark or quiet with emission control, jam enemies to deny locks, or burn through their jammers. Sensor and jammer pods are in prototype.
Morale: ambushes, unseen fire, losses and a lost flagship shake ships. Shaken groups go quiet, broken ones pull back against orders, and routed ones flee.
Campaign sensor cone: sweep space with a directional cone aimed with the right mouse button and shaped by stance, with no burn penalty. Tracked fleets start battles partly identified, and cone sweeps can start planet surveys.
Enemy cones: patrols sweep their own cones by faction doctrine (Hegemony watch, pirates hunt, Tri-Tachyon scout). Being painted gives you away, so go dark, jam them or fight.

Coming next
Cones that bend around terrain (planet shadows, nebula and storm jamming), NPC reactions to being painted, a cone UI panel, covert drop-zone raids, deception pods and decoys, more expedition types, and a balance pass.

AI use disclaimer

AI use disclaimer
This mod is developed with AI agent assistance:
Code: written by Claude (Anthropic) and Grok (xAI) agents under my direction, tested in a headless Starsector install.
Art: unit, building and tileset sprites are rendered by a procedural Python pipeline (vector shapes, shading and animation frames) written by the same agents. No image-generation model was used for sprites.
Design: mechanics and rules are mine; the agents implement and iterate on them.

Credits: LazyLib and Nexerelin authors. A balanced map starts companion mod is also in progress.
